summary: Quick scoping to align POC timeline, access gating, benchmark metrics (latency/throughput/quality), and exec readout schedule. Main risks: VPC peering timing and dataset access. Success criteria draft: p99 latency under 300ms for short prompts, end-to-end throughput 200 reqs/s at 4k tokens workload with acceptable quality scores vs baseline.
topics: Kickoff objectives; Access & networking (staging); Benchmark plan and metrics; Workload sizing and quantization profile; Mid-point review and exec readout; Security/Compliance asks; Next steps and owners.
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone thanks for hopping on. I think we have about an hour, quick intros?
[00:06] Marisol Ramos: Hi all Marisol, head of ML at Zenwave.
[00:09] Derek Lin: Derek, platform, I'll own the infra bits.
[00:11] Priya Nair: Priya from Redwood, I'll lead the benchmark plan and run the tests.
[00:14] Sana Kapoor: Sana product — hi.
[00:16] Omar Hossain: Omar, security.
[00:18] Alex Chen: Great. High-level goal: run a 6-week POC to evaluate performance, cost, and ops fit for inference. Today we'll agree milestones: kickoff, staging access, mid-point, exec readout. Also lock down success criteria.
[00:33] Marisol Ramos: Sounds good. For context our main workloads are twofold: 1) short-query semantic search and prompt-completion use for customer support (avg 120 tokens) and 2) a longer summarization flow (2–3k tokens). We want to know tail latency and cost per 1k tokens.
[00:50] Priya Nair: Good, that'll let us size batch and KV cache. For short queries we usually track p50/p95/p99 and token/sec. What are your current baseline numbers?
[01:02] Marisol Ramos: Right now on our self-hosted endpoints we see p99 around 450–550ms for small prompts at low concurrency, and the cost is... well, high.
[01:12] Alex Chen: Okay rough baseline. For this POC our suggested success criteria draft: p99 < 300ms for short prompts, throughput 150–250 reqs/s for 4k token mix under dedicated staging, and quality parity within 5% of your baseline eval metrics. Open to adjust.
[01:29] Derek Lin: That p99 target seems aggressive but reasonable if we use dedicated pools. What's the plan for access? We have a strict VPC policy.
[01:36] Priya Nair: Two options: 1) VPC peering from your staging VPC into Redwood Private staging (we'll need peering CIDRs and IAM service account), or 2) temporary secure tunnel with port-restricted bastion for the run. VPC peering is preferred for realistic latencies.
[01:52] Derek Lin: Peering is fine but needs ticket in our infra queue — can we agree on a window?
[01:56] Alex Chen: If you can open the ticket today we can aim to have peering done within 3 business days. We'll also need a service account with S3 read for the sample dataset (anonymized).
[02:08] Marisol Ramos: We'll anonymize and share 10k sample prompts plus the longer summarization set.
[02:12] Sana Kapoor: About success criteria, product care about quality — what metric are you proposing for quality parity?
[02:18] Priya Nair: We typically run an eval harness — BLEU/ROUGE variants for summarization or relevance NDCG@10 for search. Define a small gold set and we'll compute delta. Acceptance is within 5% relative to your current model.
[02:31] Omar Hossain: Security: we need SOC2 summary, KMS at rest, and assurances that KV cache doesn't persist customer data beyond session. Also SSO for the control plane.
[02:42] Alex Chen: Redwood will share the security whitepaper; we support customer-managed KMS for Private and audit logs. For Hosted we have retention controls and a KV cache life-cycle policy; we'll document that.
[02:55] Derek Lin: Good. Now benchmarks: Priya can you walk through the benchmark plan?
[02:58] Priya Nair: Sure. Phase 1 is microbenchmarks: measure single-token throughput, kernel-level latency, quantization toggles. Phase 2 is workload replay using your 10k samples at variable concurrency (1, 10, 50, 200). Phase 3 is long-run stability: 24–48h soak to validate memory/throughput and observe degradation. We'll capture p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, GPU util, and cost per 1k tokens.
[03:31] Marisol Ramos: For concurrency, our spike pattern is bursty — 0 to 200 typical, so include a burst test.
[03:38] Priya Nair: Yep burst and steady-state. We'll also test cache hit scenarios to estimate benefits of prefix caching.
[03:45] Alex Chen: On quantization — will you want 8-bit/4-bit tests? That impacts quality.
[03:49] Marisol Ramos: Yes please. We want accuracy vs cost tradeoffs.
[03:52] Priya Nair: We'll run FP16, 8-bit, and an aggressive 4-bit QAT-like run and report deltas.
[03:58] Sana Kapoor: Timeline? You said 6 weeks earlier, can you give a milestone map?
[04:02] Alex Chen: Proposed: Week 0 (this week) kickoff and access gating; Week 1 get peering + dataset + baseline capture; Week 2 microbench and quantization matrix; Week 3 workload replay and first mid-point demo; Week 4–5 extended soak and tuning; Week 6 exec readout with final recommendations. Mid-point review is critical to decide if we need to widen model variants or scale to dedicated capacity.
[04:28] Derek Lin: If peering takes longer it pushes everything. Can mid-point be flexible + we'll batch the soak after peering?
[04:34] Alex Chen: Yes, we'll keep dates fluid but try to meet Week 3 midpoint. If peering misses the slot we can do a remote tunnel for early tests but note the latency will be different — we'll flag that in the report.
[04:46] Omar Hossain: Also need an inventory of data handlers. We can't put PII in the test set.
[04:50] Marisol Ramos: We'll scrub PII and share sample.
[04:53] Priya Nair: Regarding metrics collection, we'll provide a spreadsheet template — latency histograms, GPU metrics, cost per run, quality metrics. We'll ask you to run an initial baseline on your side if possible.
[05:05] Marisol Ramos: We can run baseline for a small set this week.
[05:08] Alex Chen: Great. On tooling: we'll use our benchmark harness (a lightweight runner) — Priya will share the repo and a docker image.
[05:16] Priya Nair: I'll include runbook steps: how to authenticate, how to run with VPC peering, and how to push logs to your S3. Also note some names get transcribed wrong in this call — K-V cache sometimes comes out as k-v cash, apologies in advance.
[05:30] Sana Kapoor: (laughs) Noted. Reminder: exec readout needs a 20-minute slide deck with cost tradeoffs.
[05:36] Alex Chen: We'll prepare a template with key slides: baseline vs POC, latency/throughput, cost per 1k tokens, quantization tradeoffs, and recommended rollout plan.
[05:45] Derek Lin: For the recommended rollout, can you include autoscaling suggestions and a failover plan to a smaller model?
[05:50] Priya Nair: Yep. We'll propose autoscale policies and fallback variants — e.g., route to a lower-cost quantized model on overload, or region fallback.
[05:58] Omar Hossain: On compliance: we need a binding statement for logs retention and audit export for the pilot.
[06:02] Alex Chen: We'll include retention SLAs and an audit export step in the runbook.
[06:07] Marisol Ramos: Anything else?
[06:09] Priya Nair: Quick clarification on success criteria: do you want strict gate (must-meet) or advisory?
[06:13] Marisol Ramos: Exec cares about latency and cost. Let's make latency + quality required gates, cost advisory but modeled in scenarios.
[06:22] Alex Chen: Noted: latency and quality = pass/fail gates. Cost = scenario analysis.
[06:27] Sana Kapoor: Who will present at the mid-point?
[06:29] Alex Chen: Priya will run the mid-point demo, Alex will do exec readout with a summary slide. Marisol you indicated execs will attend the final readout?
[06:38] Marisol Ramos: Yes senior PM + CTO likely for the exec readout.
[06:41] Alex Chen: Great. Recap and owners: Priya shares benchmark template + harness by Tuesday; Derek to provision peering; Marisol to share sample data; Alex to send cost estimate and deck template.
[06:55] Derek Lin: One more infra note: if we do private deployment later we need an offline install checklist — not for this POC but please include a stub.
[07:02] Priya Nair: We'll include an on-prem/private checklist appendix.
[07:06] Alex Chen: Okay unless there are other questions we’ll wrap. Thanks everyone.
[07:11] Omar Hossain: Thanks.
[07:12] Marisol Ramos: Thanks all.
[07:13] Sana Kapoor: Thanks.
[07:15] Alex Chen: I'll follow up with the notes and action items.
[07:18] [meeting ends]
notes: Key risks: VPC peering delay, dataset anonymization, quantization quality degradation. Success gates: latency and quality. Mid-point week 3 demo determines whether to expand scope. Exec readout week 6. Redwoods to supply benchmark harness and security docs.
attachments: Benchmark template (will be shared), Security whitepaper (to follow), Runbook repo link (to follow)
